Ben / Laura / Hannah —

Thanks for the materials. Quick read-through and initial feedback below before we do line-by-line redlines: 

1) SCCs: We can accept the standard EU Commission SCCs but HealthLynx needs a short mapping table that shows which subprocessor locations will rely on which SCC clauses (we use that for our internal audit). Can Redwood supply that mapping or confirm you will include it in the TIA?

2) Role mapping: We agree Redwood is processor for the Order Form scope that covers inference-only APIs. For the training dataset scenario (if enabled later), we will need controller/processor clarifications — please flag in the Order Form where training is optional.

3) Technical evidence: We will request KMS region guarantees for keys used with customer-managed KMS. Please confirm Redwood's supported KMS regions and whether HSM-backed keys are available as an add-on.

4) Pricing: If the TIA requires onshore-only routing or additional contractual guarantees (e.g., dedicated instance routing), expect a pricing impact. We will hold off on final PO until legal signs off.

Action: Oliver will circulate HealthLynx's redlines by end of day Thursday 12/11. Julia will coordinate procurement.

Ben / Team / HealthLynx —

Thanks for the input, Oliver. A few internal notes and proposed language we want HealthLynx to consider in their redlines: 

- SCC mapping: We can provide a 1-page exhibit that maps subprocessor-hosted regions to the SCC references and the list of subprocessors. Deliverable: Redwood will include "Exhibit X: Subprocessor & SCC mapping" if HealthLynx confirms acceptance of SCC templates (no changes).

- Role clarity in Order Form: Proposed insertion (Order Form, Exhibit A): "Customer-selected features that enable model training or persistent customer model artifacts shall be explicitly listed; absent such selection, Redwood remains processor for API inference only." This avoids scope creep.

- KMS / HSM: We support HSM-backed keys in select regions (EU-West, US-East). We will provide a KMS region table in the Drive link and an ops runbook for key rotation/evidence. HSM availability is an add-on and will be reflected in Pricing Schedule (Order Form, Section 3).

- Transfer-impact addendum (TIA): If HealthLynx requests a TIA documenting residual transfer risk mitigation beyond SCCs, that will trigger a change in the timeline (approx +7 business days) and may require minor pricing uplift for dedicated routing. Suggest we keep the TIA request explicit in their redlines so we can scope it.

Commercial ask to Ben: If HealthLynx asks for dedicated routing or onshore-only routing, prepare two impact scenarios (tech + $): (1) Soft assurance (SCCs + routing preferences) — minimal cost; (2) Strong assurance (dedicated routing / reserved capacity) — material uplift and procurement approval.

I'll prepare tracked language for the three clauses above and upload before our review call. Can we set a 30-minute working session tomorrow 12/12 at 10:00am CET to walk the redlines with HealthLynx legal? Ben — can you confirm availability and send calendar invite?

Laura Bennett
